nodes.name: Trace context
nodes.notes: Joins the caller's W3C trace: n8n's built-in OpenTelemetry spans use the inbound traceparent too, so the LLM steps below land in the SAME Langfuse trace as the workflow and node spans.

nodes.name: Get prompt (Langfuse)
nodes.notes: Official Langfuse node (prompt management): fetches the version labelled `production`. The model and temperature come from the prompt's config.

nodes.name: Mask PII
nodes.notes: Masks card numbers (Luhn-checked), IBANs, e-mails and phone numbers BEFORE the text reaches the model or Langfuse.

nodes.name: Classify complaint
nodes.notes: System prompt, model and temperature come from the Langfuse prompt. Simplify Output is OFF so the response keeps `model` and `usage` (token counts) for the trace.

options.system:
You are a customer-care agent at Northwind Bank (a fictional retail bank). Write a short, empathetic reply (at most 120 words) to the customer's complaint.
Rules:
- Never ask for full card numbers, PINs, passwords or one-time codes.
- If the category is card_fraud: say the card has been blocked as a precaution and that the 24/7 fraud team (number on the back of the card) will review the transactions.
- If regulatory escalation is true: say the complaint is logged as a formal complaint and a written response follows within 15 business days.
- Do not promise refunds or compensation.
- Sign as "Northwind Customer Care".

nodes.name: Build Langfuse trace
nodes.notes: Builds an OTLP/JSON payload: root observation + PII guardrail + two LLM generations (model, tokens, prompt link). Langfuse computes cost from model + tokens.

nodes.name: Send trace to Langfuse
nodes.notes: POSTs the spans to Langfuse's OTLP endpoint after the customer already has the answer. Uses the same Langfuse credential as the prompt node (Basic auth). On failure the run continues.
